finding.claim: Authorization bypass: the ban endpoint swallows the 403 raised by require_admin, so any authenticated non-admin user can ban arbitrary users.
finding.source: Any authenticated non-admin user sending POST /admin/users/<uid>/ban with an arbitrary uid
finding.sink: do_ban(uid) at admin.py:20, a privileged admin operation

trace.note: ban(uid) handler is entered with attacker-controlled uid and g.user lacking is_admin
abort(403) raises werkzeug HTTPException, a subclass of Exception
the handler only logs a warning and does not return or re-raise
execution falls through to do_ban(uid), which runs for the non-admin

finding.guards_checked: require_admin is the only guard and is neutralized by the broad except. There is no return or re-raise in the except block. No other auth decorator or before_request hook exists in the file. The sibling unban route calls require_admin without a try/except, so it is correctly protected.

verdict.guard_found: require_admin (admin.py:9-11) aborts with 403 on failure, but the call at admin.py:17 is wrapped in try/except Exception (16-19) that only logs and falls through. No route decorator or before_request hook exists in the file.
verdict.reason: At admin.py:17-20, the 403 from require_admin (line 11) is caught by `except Exception` at line 18, which only logs at line 19 with no return or re-raise, so do_ban(uid) at line 20 runs for any non-admin; the unban route at admin.py:26 is unguarded by try/except and so is protected.
